season_storylines: Bijan Robinson (ATL) and Jahmyr Gibbs (DET) are both sitting out training camp practices seeking new contracts, and in a non-PPR league where their TD-plus-yardage profiles are top-5 assets, any hold-in that bleeds into September adds early-week risk to first-round picks.

The QB carousel reset half the league: Tua Tagovailoa was traded to Atlanta and has taken most first-team reps over Michael Penix Jr. under new HC Kevin Stefanski, Kyler Murray was traded to Minnesota and is expected to beat out J.J. McCarthy, Kirk Cousins signed with the Raiders and should start over rookie Fernando Mendoza, and Geno Smith signed with the Jets, so late-round QB values hinge on these camps.

Cleveland is splitting first-team reps between Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson in a true open competition, which suppresses every Browns pass catcher until it resolves and is the main reason Harold Fannin Jr. is a repeat-risk at his price.

A massive WR reshuffle moved A.J. Brown to New England, DJ Moore to Buffalo, Jaylen Waddle to Denver, Michael Pittman Jr. to Pittsburgh and Mike Evans to San Francisco, creating target-and-TD vacuums that elevate DeVonta Smith in Philadelphia, Luther Burden III in Chicago and Emeka Egbuka in Tampa.

Josh Jacobs faces an open domestic-violence investigation with a realistic six-plus game suspension outcome if charged conduct is confirmed (verify), which combined with his age-28, 2,100-touch decline makes MarShawn Lloyd one of the cheapest contingent-value RB stashes in drafts.

Malik Nabers had a second offseason knee procedure to clean up his ACL repair and reporting points to a Week 5-6 return (verify), and since his game is catch volume he loses even more relative value in a zero-PPR format.

Matthew Stafford is coming off an age-37 MVP season with 46 TDs on a career-high 7.7 percent TD rate, and in a 6-pt-passing-TD league that exact stat is the regression trap: he adds nothing rushing and is being drafted at his ceiling.

Rookie draft capital landed in fantasy-friendly spots: Jeremiyah Love went third overall to Arizona as a three-down back, Jadarian Price went 32nd to Seattle where Zach Charbonnet's ACL recovery clears a feature role, Carnell Tate gives Tennessee a contested-catch X receiver, and Jordyn Tyson joins a motion-heavy Saints scheme.

Betting markets frame the TD environment: Baltimore and the Rams sit atop the board at 11.5 wins while Arizona (3.5), Miami (4.5) and Cleveland/Vegas/Jets (5.5) anchor the bottom, so TD-dependent assets on those bottom offenses need a volume excuse to draft.

Baker Mayfield says he feels disrespected by Tampa Bay's extension offer, wants roughly 50 million per year and will not negotiate in-season, a situation worth monitoring but not yet a practice holdout.

teams.outlook: New HC Mike LaFleur brings a McVay-tree scheme but Kyler Murray was traded away and the league-low 3.5 win total caps team TD volume, so third-overall rookie RB Jeremiyah Love's projected workload is the one asset that survives the environment.

Kevin Stefanski takes over with Tua Tagovailoa (working through a back flare-up) ahead of Penix, and his run/TE-friendly system points TD equity at Bijan Robinson once the contract standoff ends, with Kyle Pitts a buzzy but repeatedly disappointing bet.

New OC Declan Doyle (Ben Johnson tree) installs a motion-and-shot-play offense for the board-high 11.5-win roster, a bounce-back setup for Lamar Jackson's rushing-plus-6pt-TD ceiling and Zay Flowers, with age-32 Derrick Henry the TD-dependent piece.

Trading for DJ Moore finally gives Josh Allen a true alpha on a 10.5-win offense, boosting Allen's already elite rushing-TD floor and making Moore's yardage-and-TD profile a better non-PPR buy than his recent catch-volume seasons suggest.

Rookie WR Chris Brazzell II's LCL tear ends his season and Jonathon Brooks is finally cleared, so Tetairoa McMillan consolidates targets while Chuba Hubbard's grip on goal-line work is now genuinely contested (verify).

Ben Johnson's offense enters year two with roughly 150 targets vacated by DJ Moore and Olamide Zaccheaus leaving, and with Rome Odunze managing a foot issue, Luther Burden III's elite per-route efficiency makes him the TD-and-yardage breakout of the receiver class.

The Bengals spent on defense (Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen) rather than the offense, which keeps the Burrow-to-Chase TD pipeline intact at a 10.5-win total and keeps Chase the safest non-PPR WR1 profile in the league.

Todd Monken's arrival helps RBs and TEs but the Sanders-vs-Watson QB split and a 5.5-win total suppress the passing tree, leaving Quinshon Judkins's early-down and goal-line role as the only Browns asset priced to profit.

Dallas projects near the top of the league in passing yards and TDs with Dak Prescott healthy, Jaydon Blue is winning the RB2 job with pass-game buzz, and the WR depth behind the starters (Ryan Flournoy) is cheap TD exposure.

Trading for Jaylen Waddle gives Bo Nix a legit separator in Sean Payton's offense at a 9.5-win total, though Nix's own fantasy case still leans on the run game and his modest rushing contribution rather than big passing volume.

Jahmyr Gibbs's contract hold-in is the story, and Detroit signing Isiah Pacheco gives the Lions a credible early-down hedge that trims Gibbs's goal-line certainty at his first-round price until a deal is signed.

Josh Jacobs's legal jeopardy plus late-2025 decline opens the door for MarShawn Lloyd, while Tucker Kraft tracking toward a Week 1 return from his torn ACL (verify) restores a red-zone TD target for Jordan Love.

C.J. Stroud extension talks are positive and the rebuilt line (Braden Smith, Wyatt Teller) plus David Montgomery point to a rhythm offense where Nico Collins stays the alpha and Jayden Higgins inherits the Christian Kirk targets with real TD equity.

Trading Michael Pittman Jr. strips catch-volume from the offense and re-centers it on Jonathan Taylor's rushing TDs at a modest 7.5-win total, with the remaining receiver pecking order genuinely unsettled (verify).

Travis Etienne Jr.'s departure hands Bhayshul Tuten a lead role after he posted 7 TDs on 93 touches and a near-best missed-tackle rate as a rookie, making him a clean non-PPR RB2 bet in Liam Coen's run game.

Kansas City signed Kenneth Walker III to replace Pacheco and traded Trent McDuffie away, and while Rashee Rice is available after serving jail time this spring, the market's Mahomes-regression chatter matters less in a 6-pt-passing league where his TD volume still clears.

New OC Mike McDaniel installs the wide-zone, motion-heavy scheme that made De'Von Achane a star, a direct ceiling-raiser for Omarion Hampton and Justin Herbert, with David Njoku and Quentin Johnston as the discount TD plays if the line holds up.
An 11.5-win roster added Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie, but the fantasy angle is fading Matthew Stafford's 46-TD, 7.7-percent-TD-rate season while still trusting Puka Nacua's yardage dominance.

Klint Kubiak's RB-friendly system plus Kirk Cousins starting and a rebuilt interior line (Tyler Linderbaum) fix the league-worst blocking that buried Ashton Jeanty, making Jeanty and Brock Bowers the only Raiders worth their price at a 5.5-win total.

A teardown traded away Tua and Waddle, handed the offense to Jeff Hafley/Bobby Slowik with Malik Willis at QB and a 4.5-win total, so De'Von Achane's talent now fights a bottom-two scoring environment every week.

Kyler Murray arrives via trade and should start over J.J. McCarthy, pairing his rushing floor and 6-pt passing TDs with Justin Jefferson in Kevin O'Connell's system - a sneaky QB1 path if the fit clicks (verify).

Trading for A.J. Brown gives Drake Maye a contested-catch alpha on a 10.5-win offense, concentrating TD equity in Brown while the crowded secondary receiver room (Doubs, Douglas, Boutte, Williams) stays a fantasy dead zone.

Tyler Shough closed 2025 with six straight 17-plus point games and a top-two rate of carries inside the 10, and adding rookie Jordyn Tyson plus Travis Etienne to a motion-heavy scheme makes the Saints' cheap pieces quietly playable despite a 7.5-win total.

A new staff with OC Matt Nagy (verify) builds around Jaxson Dart, whose 9 rushing TDs in 12 starts is exactly what 6-pt-TD non-PPR leagues pay for, while Malik Nabers's Week 5-6 knee timeline (verify) shifts early-season TD work to Cam Skattebo and Theo Johnson.

Geno Smith projects bottom-third in passing volume on a 5.5-win team, so Garrett Wilson's target share is safer than his TD total, and rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq's promised big role mostly cannibalizes Mason Taylor rather than creating new value.

A.J. Brown's trade to New England leaves DeVonta Smith an uncontested No. 1, and first-time play-caller Sean Mannion's Shanahan-tree scheme talks up Saquon Barkley's receiving role, though Barkley's own post-mega-workload risk is real.

Mike McCarthy as HC means more pass volume for Aaron Rodgers to DK Metcalf and the newly acquired Michael Pittman Jr., while Rico Dowdle's power style is expected to beat out Jaylen Warren for the lead and goal-line work.
Zach Charbonnet's ACL recovery delays him significantly, clearing first-rounder Jadarian Price for feature-back duties on a 10.5-win offense where Jaxon Smith-Njigba remains the yardage engine.

Kyle Shanahan's offense is a minefield of recovery bets: Christian McCaffrey is coming off roughly 450 touches, George Kittle is pushing an aggressive Week 1 return from a January Achilles tear, Mike Evans arrives at age 33, Ricky Pearsall has recurring PCL swelling, and Brandon Aiyuk may not play at all (verify).

New OC Zac Robinson's McVay-tree scheme plus Mike Evans's departure make Emeka Egbuka a top-10 WR bet, with the backfield split between Bucky Irving (returning from shoulder surgery) and Kenneth Gainwell, and Baker Mayfield's contract standoff simmering in the background.

Robert Saleh hired Brian Daboll to run the offense, and Daboll's RPO/play-action system plus rookie Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson set up Cam Ward for a year-two leap even with a 6.5-win total, while the Pollard/Spears/Singleton backfield stays a committee to avoid.

Jayden Daniels's rushing keeps him a locked-in top-tier QB in this format regardless of the 7.5-win total, and rookie Antonio Williams plus Chig Okonkwo fill the target void behind Terry McLaurin without threatening him.

breakout_watch.name: Luther Burden III
breakout_watch.why: Ben Johnson's Bears vacated about 150 targets (DJ Moore, Zaccheaus gone) and Burden posted a 2.92 YPRR rookie season; his after-catch, big-play profile is yardage-and-TD driven, exactly what non-PPR rewards, at a WR28-ish price.

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Mike McDaniel's wide-zone Chargers scheme produced consecutive elite RB seasons for Achane, and Hampton flashed RB1 weeks before his 2025 ankle fracture; a healthy year-two workload carries rushing-TD upside far above ADP.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Etienne's exit makes him the Jaguars' lead back after 7 TDs on 93 rookie touches and a top-two missed-tackle-forced rate; goal-line-inclusive volume in a decent offense is gold at 10 yards per point.

breakout_watch.name: Jadarian Price
breakout_watch.why: Round 1 pick 32 in Seattle with Charbonnet's ACL recovery significantly delayed, on a 10.5-win offense; a rookie feature back with breakaway speed and a clear path is the cleanest volume bet in this class.

breakout_watch.name: Jeremiyah Love
breakout_watch.why: Third overall picks at RB have overwhelmingly finished top-12; Arizona's 3.5-win environment caps team TDs but his three-down role means he IS the offense, and yardage volume travels in non-PPR.

breakout_watch.name: Emeka Egbuka
breakout_watch.why: Mike Evans's departure vacates the Bucs' red-zone alpha role; Egbuka already posted 938 yards and 6 TDs as a rookie and Zac Robinson's McVay-tree scheme funnels TD equity to the lead receiver.

breakout_watch.name: Jaxson Dart
breakout_watch.why: 9 rushing TDs in 12 starts as a rookie is a cheat code at 6 points per TD; even modest passing growth under Matt Nagy makes him a weekly QB1 by rushing floor alone.

breakout_watch.name: Cam Ward
breakout_watch.why: Brian Daboll's arrival plus rookie X receiver Carnell Tate and slot Wan'Dale Robinson give Ward a real year-two leap setup; his aggressive downfield profile fits 25-yards-per-point passing scoring.

breakout_watch.name: Tyler Shough
breakout_watch.why: Six straight games of 17-plus points to close 2025 and the second-highest rate of QB carries inside the 10 - short-TD equity at 6 points each - plus rookie Jordyn Tyson added to a motion-heavy scheme.

breakout_watch.name: Ashton Jeanty
breakout_watch.why: Ranked dead last among 80 RBs in yards before contact as a rookie; Klint Kubiak's RB-friendly scheme and a rebuilt interior line (Linderbaum) fix the blocking, not the player, so the year-two spike is infrastructure-driven.

breakout_watch.name: Jayden Higgins
breakout_watch.why: Matched Nico Collins with 6 TDs as a rookie, Christian Kirk is gone and Collins has an injury history; Higgins's size/athleticism profile is a red-zone TD play, not a slot compiler, ideal for zero-PPR.

breakout_watch.name: MarShawn Lloyd
breakout_watch.why: Finally healthy and one Josh Jacobs suspension or continued decline away from lead-back touches in a 9.5-win Green Bay offense; contingent goal-line value at a near-free ADP of 180.

breakout_watch.name: Quentin Johnston
breakout_watch.why: Clear No. 2 behind McConkey in McDaniel's new Chargers offense with a downfield, TD-leaning role; deep-threat spike weeks beat slot volume in this format and he costs a mid-round pick.

breakout_watch.name: Jordyn Tyson
breakout_watch.why: Saints rookie landing in the league's most motion-heavy, schemed-open passing game with Tyler Shough ascending; his vertical juice gives him non-PPR spike-week value immediately (verify draft capital).

fade_watch.name: Matthew Stafford
fade_watch.why: 46 TDs on a career-high 7.7 percent TD rate at age 38 is the textbook regression profile, and in a 6-pt-passing-TD league his value is entirely that TD total; zero rushing means no floor when it normalizes.

fade_watch.name: Christian McCaffrey
fade_watch.why: Coming off roughly 450 touches at age 30, and history is brutal to workhorses the year after that workload; his reception-heavy usage is also discounted to zero in non-PPR.

fade_watch.name: Josh Jacobs
fade_watch.why: Age 28 with 2,100-plus career touches, efficiency already slipping (4.0 YPC, sharp late-2025 fade), and an open domestic-violence investigation with realistic six-game suspension risk (verify outcome).

fade_watch.name: Mike Evans
fade_watch.why: Age-33 season on a new team after missing nine games with a career-low scoring pace; only a couple of receivers in a decade have returned top-25 value at that age, and his price still reflects the old TD machine.

fade_watch.name: Malik Nabers
fade_watch.why: Second knee procedure this offseason with a reported Week 5-6 return (verify); he's a target-volume player whose catches are worth nothing here, so paying a top-50 pick for a partial yardage season is negative EV.

fade_watch.name: Derrick Henry
fade_watch.why: Age-32 with massive career mileage on a team that just changed offensive systems; his value is purely TD-dependent now, and any goal-line erosion under a new play-caller craters him.

fade_watch.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
fade_watch.why: Career-best everything in 2025 with Njoku gone, but the Sanders/Watson QB mess, a 5.5-win total, defenses adjusting and reported light offseason work make a repeat at his elevated ADP unlikely.

fade_watch.name: De'Von Achane
fade_watch.why: Mike McDaniel, the scheme that made him, is now in LA; Miami's 4.5-win total and Malik Willis at QB mean stacked boxes and few scoring drives, so his TD and big-play rates should compress hard.

fade_watch.name: Rashee Rice
fade_watch.why: Served jail time in May with league discipline believed exhausted (verify), but he is a short-area, catch-volume receiver - the exact archetype non-PPR discounts - priced on PPR reputation.

fade_watch.name: Kyle Pitts
fade_watch.why: The Stefanski-revival narrative is real enough to inflate his price again, but he has never sustained TD production and Atlanta's 6.5-win total plus a run-first identity cap the scoring chances that this format needs from him.

uncertainty_note: Most unsettled right now: the Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs contract standoffs (both sat out July 29 practice with no resolution timeline), the Cleveland QB split between Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson, Josh Jacobs's open legal investigation and any league discipline, Malik Nabers's actual return week after his second knee procedure, Arizona's starting QB plan after the Kyler Murray trade, Brandon Aiyuk's status in San Francisco, and the Baker Mayfield extension standoff; several secondary depth-chart reports conflict across outlets this week (e.g., Adonai Mitchell's and Greg Dulcich's exact teams, Tampa Bay's RB pecking order), so treat late-round role claims as fluid until preseason games.
